🏆 Today's Activity – Topic Presentation 🎤

"Speak on What Inspires You!"

🎯 Students will present a 4-slide PowerPoint on a topic of their choice, sharing insights, ideas, or information in an engaging and structured way.

🎯 Each student will have 3 minutes to present.

‼ For Students Who Have a Specific Topic in Mind:
Your presentation should include:

📌 Slide 1: Title & Introduction – What is your topic and why did you choose it?

📌 Slide 2: Background/Context – Provide some basic information or context about the topic.

📌 Slide 3: Key Insights – Share 2–3 interesting or important points related to your topic.

📌 Slide 4: Your Thoughts – What are your views or takeaways? Why is this topic important or relevant?

‼ For Students Who Are Still Exploring Topics:
If you're unsure or still exploring, present on something you're curious about or learning recently:

📌 What drew your interest to this area?
📌 What have you found out so far?
📌 What do you hope to learn more about?

 ✅ Guidelines:

⏳ Duration:  3 minutes per student
📂 Format: PowerPoint (4 slides)
🎯 Focus: Clear, concise, and confidently delivered presentation

✨ Choose a topic you’re passionate or curious about — and make it your moment to shine!

sourceText:
How to compute sample size using G*Power for the following study?
The study will be conducted using a 1x3 between-subjects design (n=120) with the independent variable “Visualization Type” with the levels VR, 2D, and None. The study participants will hence be divided into three groups and undergo either of the three levels. They will be asked to fill out questionnaires at the beginning and the end of the study, which will record their personality traits, psychological well-being, and self-reported public speaking anxiety. 

During the study, the participants will give two speeches and will be asked to fill out pre- and post-speech questionnaires regarding their public speaking anxiety level and perceived performance. We will record their physiological data throughout the study. Additionally, we will record their speeches to extract speech metrics and record their speech videos to extract their non-verbal behaviors like hand, head, and body movement. At the end of the study, we will conduct a short interview to gather subjective feedback from the participants about their experience of the respective condition.
